questions.q: In physics, how do the terms distance and displacement differ?
options: Distance is a vector with direction, while displacement is a scalar with magnitude only
Distance describes the total length of the pathway taken (a scalar quantity), while displacement indicates the change in position relative to the starting location and is a vector quantity
Distance and displacement are interchangeable and always have the same value
Displacement is always greater than distance for any journey
questions.explanation: Distance is the total length of the pathway taken and is a scalar - magnitude only. Displacement gives the location of the destination relative to the start, irrespective of the path, and is a vector with both magnitude and direction. For a closed loop the displacement is zero while the distance is not.

questions.q: On a velocity-versus-time graph, what does the area under the graph represent?
options: The acceleration of the object during that interval
The displacement of the object during the interval represented by that part of the graph
The instantaneous velocity of the object
The total distance, never the displacement
questions.explanation: The area under any part of the velocity-versus-time graph is equal to the displacement during the interval. For Steady Sam, the area of the rectangle under the graph is 15 s x 6.7 m s-1 = 100 m, his displacement. Area above the time axis is positive displacement, area below is negative.

questions.q: What does the gradient of a velocity-versus-time graph represent?
options: The displacement of the object
The acceleration, because the gradient is a measure of the rate of change of velocity
The total distance travelled
The instantaneous position of the object
questions.explanation: The gradient of a velocity-versus-time graph is a measure of the rate of change of velocity, just as the gradient of a position-versus-time graph measures the rate of change of position. For the elevator in interval A, the gradient (rise over run) is +8.0 m s-1 / 5.0 s = +1.6 m s-2.

questions.q: A coin is dropped into a wishing well and accelerates towards the water at a constant 9.8 m s-2. It takes 3.0 s to reach the water. How far does the coin fall before hitting the water?
working: \(s = ut + \tfrac{1}{2}at^2\)  (this equation omits the final velocity \(v\))
questions.explanation: From rest u = 0, so with constant acceleration use s = ut + half a t squared, which includes the three known quantities (u, a, t) and the unknown s. The coin falls about 44 m.

questions.q: A car skidded in a straight line for 2.0 s with constant deceleration, leaving a skid mark of length 12 m before stopping. At what speed was the car travelling as it began to skid? (Take forward as positive, so v = 0.)
questions.explanation: The acceleration is missing and not needed, so use s = half (u + v) t. With v = 0 this gives u = 12 m s-1. The car was travelling at 12 m s-1, about 43 km h-1, as it began to skid.

questions.q: A vector of magnitude R at polar angle theta is resolved into its horizontal and vertical components. What are those components?
options: \(R_x = R\sin\theta\),  \(R_y = R\cos\theta\)
\(R_x = R\cos\theta\),  \(R_y = R\sin\theta\)
\(R_x = R\tan\theta\),  \(R_y = R\)
\(R_x = R/\cos\theta\),  \(R_y = R/\sin\theta\)
questions.explanation: Using polar angles, Rx = R cos theta and Ry = R sin theta. All vectors in two dimensions can be considered as the sum of an independent horizontal and vertical component. In words: adjacent is cosine, opposite is sine.

questions.q: In your own words, state the rule for the relative velocity of an object as measured by a moving observer.
keyPoints: Relative velocity is the velocity of an object as measured by a moving observer.
The velocity of an object B relative to an observer A is vB rel A = vB - vA.
It is a vector subtraction: you subtract the observer's velocity vector from the object's velocity vector.
questions.explanation: Relative velocity is the velocity of an object measured by a moving observer, given by vB rel A = vB - vA (the velocity of A relative to B is A minus B). For a car 15 north and a truck 10 south, the car relative to the truck is 15 - (-10) = 25 m s-1 north.

questions.q: In vector subtraction, how is the resultant of A - B found?
options: By adding the magnitudes of A and B together
The resultant of A - B = A + (-B), where (-B) has the same magnitude as B but is directed in the opposite direction
By subtracting the angle of B from the angle of A only
A - B is always zero whenever A and B are perpendicular
questions.explanation: In vector subtraction the resultant of A - B = A + (-B), where (-B) is equal in magnitude to B but directed in the opposite direction. This is how a change in velocity (v - u) is evaluated, even when only the direction changes.

questions.q: The equation v = u + at follows from the definition of constant acceleration. Why is full vector notation not strictly necessary when applying it to motion along a straight line?
options: Because acceleration is never really a vector quantity
Because along a straight line the vectors can be expressed as positive or negative quantities, so vector notation is not necessary
Because the velocity of an object has no direction
Because the equation only applies to motion in two dimensions
questions.explanation: When acceleration is constant, a = (v - u)/t rearranges to v = u + at. This is a vector equation, but as long as the motion is along a straight line the vectors can be expressed as positive or negative quantities, so vector notation is not necessary.

questions.q: Reload the module's memory hooks: recall the three motion-graph rules and the suvat missing-variable method.
keyPoints: Gradient climbs the ladder, area descends it: gradient of a displacement-time graph is velocity, gradient of a velocity-time graph is acceleration, and the area under a velocity-time graph is displacement.
D-V-A: displacement, velocity, acceleration are the vector trio that must always carry a direction (distance and speed are their scalar shadows).
SUVAT missing-variable method: name the quantity you don't have and don't need, then pick the equation that omits it.
questions.explanation: These are the brain-dump hooks from the review: the three graph rules, D-V-A, and the four suvat equations with their gaps. Writing them on the page in the first minute externalises the whole module.
